title: What must a flight training organization do to meet CASA Part 141 and Part 142?
description: CASA Part 141 and Part 142 rules for flight schools and training providers: approvals, instructor checks, training systems and record deadlines.
shortAnswer: The Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) regulates Australian flight training under two parts of the Civil Aviation Safety Regulations 1998. Part 141 covers recreational, private and commercial pilot training outside integrated courses; Part 142 covers integrated and multi-crew training and contracted training and checking for operators. Both require a CASA authorization, a qualified head of operations, instructors with a valid annual standardisation and proficiency check, and training records kept for at least 7 years.
keyTakeaways: Conducting Part 141 flight training without a Part 141 certificate or CASA approval is a strict liability offense (regulation 141.050); Part 142 activities need an AOC when conducted in an aircraft or a Part 142 certificate in a flight simulation training device (regulation 142.050).
Instructors must hold a valid standardisation and proficiency check for the operator, valid to the end of the month of completion plus 12 months (regulations 141.190 and 142.325).

Part 141 operators must record each training session within 7 days and give the student a copy within 7 days; Part 142 operators must record participation and an assessment of performance within 21 days.
Part 142 operators must run a training management system, an internal training and checking system and either a safety management system or a quality assurance management system.
A Part 142 head of operations must hold a flight examiner rating and, where training involves multi-crew operations, an air transport pilot licence (regulation 142.185).
regulator: Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA), under Parts 141 and 142 of the Civil Aviation Safety Regulations 1998
appliesTo: Flight schools conducting recreational, private and commercial pilot training (Part 141 operators)
Integrated pilot training providers, type rating and multi-crew training organizations (Part 142 operators)
Organizations conducting contracted training or checking for air operators
Heads of operations, instructors and examiners working for these organizations

sections.heading: Does an organization need Part 141 or Part 142?

blocks.text: The kind of training decides the Part. Part 141 is titled "Recreational, private and commercial pilot flight training, other than certain integrated training courses." Part 142 is titled "Integrated and multi-crew pilot flight training, contracted training and contracted checking." Both sit in Volume 4 of the [Civil Aviation Safety Regulations 1998](https://www.legislation.gov.au/F1998B00220/2026-09-29/2026-09-29/text/original/pdf/4).

Regulation 142.015 defines Part 142 flight training to include integrated courses for a private or commercial pilot licence; training for a multi-crew pilot licence, air transport pilot licence or flight engineer licence; multi-crew cooperation training; most type rating training; and certain training conducted as a multi-crew operation. Regulation 142.020 adds contracted training and contracted checking, which a Part 142 operator conducts for an aircraft operator that remains responsible for it under the regulations.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects Compilation No. 103 of CASR (compilation date September 29, 2026) as at November 2026. Several requirements refer to the operator's own operations manual or exposition and to CASA legislative instruments, which should be read alongside the regulations.

sections.heading: What qualifications must the head of operations hold?

blocks.text: The head of operations is the accountable training manager in both Parts, and the qualification bar is higher in Part 142.

items: **Part 141 (regulation 141.125):** an instructor rating with either a grade 1 training endorsement under Part 61 or the training endorsements for all the Part 141 training the operator proposes, or a CASA approval. When approving, CASA may consider management experience, formal educational qualifications, experience as a trainer or educator, operational experience and flight crew qualifications, and may direct an assessment.

**Part 142 (regulation 142.185):** a flight examiner rating the person can exercise, an air transport pilot licence if any activity involves multi-crew operations, Part 61 authorization on an aircraft kind used for a significant proportion of activities, required experience, a satisfactory record in conducting or managing air operations, and sufficient safety and regulatory knowledge, or a CASA approval.

blocks.text: Regulation 141.130 makes the Part 141 head of operations responsible for ensuring training is conducted "in accordance with principles of competency-based training in a consistent and systematic manner," which links the role to curriculum and assessment design, not just flight operations. See [competency-based training](/glossary/competency-based-training).

sections.heading: What must instructors and examiners meet?

blocks.text: Instructors must hold the right Part 61 authorization and a current operator-specific check. The two Parts use parallel rules:

items: **Part 61 authorization:** instructors must be authorized under Part 61 for the training they conduct (regulations 141.175 and 142.230).

**Standardisation and proficiency check:** a Part 141 instructor must hold a valid check for the operator (141.185). A Part 142 instructor must hold one or be successfully participating in the operator's internal training and checking system (142.320).

**Validity:** the check is valid from completion to the end of that month, plus the following 12 months. A new check completed less than 3 months before expiry runs 12 months from the old expiry date (141.190 and 142.325).

**Content:** for Part 141, the check covers delivering ground briefings and flight training to the operator's syllabus, and is conducted by the head of operations or a person they authorize (141.195).

**Human factors and non-technical skills:** instructors must meet the operations manual's requirements on human factors and non-technical skills training (141.200), and Part 142 applies the same rule to instructors and examiners against the exposition (142.335).

**Simulators:** instructors (and, for Part 142, examiners) must be assessed by the operator as competent to conduct training in a flight simulation training device before using one (141.205 and 142.240).

blocks.text: Each of these offenses carries a penalty of 50 penalty units and is a strict liability offense, so an expired check is a compliance breach for the operator on the first lesson after expiry. An annual check cycle is a natural fit for [verification of competency](/guides/how-to-set-up-verification-of-competency) records.

sections.heading: What systems must a Part 142 operator run?

blocks.text: A Part 142 operator must document its training design, its staff checking and its safety or quality assurance in formal systems described in its exposition.

items: **Training management system (142.255):** for each kind of flight training or contracted training, a course outline, detailed syllabus, standards to be met and record forms; procedures when a standard is not met; and an auditable system for records of results.

**Internal training and checking system (142.315):** how internal training and checking is conducted, duties of those who conduct it, procedures so each person understands the training management system and is supervised, command responsibility, minimum check pilots, standards to be achieved, training sequences for common faults, methods of simulating emergencies, and procedures to keep instructor checks valid.
**Safety management system (142.265):** required where activities use aircraft; it must identify and address deficiencies in training outcomes and integrate human factors principles.
**Quality assurance management system (142.270):** required where activities use only flight simulation training devices.

**Exposition (142.340):** must describe the program for training and assessing personnel in human factors principles and non-technical skills, and name the instructors appointed to be responsible for particular flight training.

blocks.text: Airlines contracting a Part 142 operator remain responsible for the training under their own training and checking system: see [CASA Part 121 training and checking](/regulations/casa-part-121-operator-training-and-checking).

sections.heading: What training records must be kept and shared?

blocks.text: Both Parts set firm deadlines for making records and keep them for at least 7 years. Under regulation 141.275, a Part 141 operator must record each session within 7 days and retain the record for at least 7 years; under 141.280, it must give the student a copy within 7 days of making it.

Under regulation 142.355, a Part 142 operator must record each person's participation in an authorized activity, "including a description and assessment of the person's performance," within 21 days, and keep it for at least 7 years. Under 142.360, records must be made available to the person on request. In both Parts, where the student has given written authority, the operator must send a copy to another operator within 7 days of a request.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry structures each syllabus as defined competencies, standards and assessment points, which is the content a Part 142 training management system must hold and a Part 141 head of operations must deliver consistently. Instructor check content can be tied to the same syllabus elements, so standardisation checks test what instructors actually teach.

faqs.q: Can a flight school conduct training without a current instructor check?
faqs.a: No. Under regulation 141.185, a Part 141 operator commits a strict liability offense, with a penalty of 50 penalty units, if an instructor conducts authorized flight training without a valid standardisation and proficiency check for that operator. The check lapses at the end of the 12 months following the month it was completed.

faqs.q: Does an airline need Part 142 to train its own pilots?
faqs.a: Not for training under its own training and checking system. Part 142 covers flight training, contracted training and contracted checking as defined in regulations 142.015 and 142.020. Contracted training is training a Part 142 operator conducts for an aircraft operator that remains responsible for it, so a third party training provider needs Part 142.

faqs.q: How quickly must a Part 142 operator record a training event?
faqs.a: Within 21 days. Regulation 142.355 requires a record of each person's participation in an authorized Part 142 activity, including a description and assessment of their performance, within 21 days of the activity. The record must be kept for at least 7 years and made available to the person on request.

faqs.q: Who can conduct a Part 141 standardisation and proficiency check?
faqs.a: Regulation 141.195 requires the check to be carried out by the operator's head of operations or by a person the head of operations has authorized. It must check the instructor's competency to deliver ground briefings and flight training in accordance with the operator's training syllabus.
